purpose: Teach: ゲーテ/プリンセス/モナコ/ボリビア/シオン/有楽町/三鷹/ダーリン

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがゲーテのファウストをご愛読された
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to read Goethe's Faust.
lines.style: Soft, reaching back into memory. Gentle opening, like turning a page carefully. Warm nostalgia in the voice, not melancholy. Slight pause before the title, as if seeing it on the spine again.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、プリンセスダイアナを追悼されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and your grandfather mourned Princess Diana, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Playful correction, gently teasing. A knowing warmth underneath. Acknowledging his memory while offering her own, side-by-side. Soft affection in 'dear,' not condescension.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがモナコのカジノに行かれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he went to the Monaco casino.
lines.style: Same reach backward, but lighter this time. A smile in the voice — not mocking, but amused by the contrast between his Faust and her casino. Wondering tone.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ボリビアの民族音楽を好まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather loved Bolivian folk music, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Quick, bright counter-memory. She's not disagreeing — she's joining in the dance. Each their own detail, equally cherished. Affectionate challenge in the rhythm.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがシオンの丘の歴史本を読まれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he read history books about Zion Hill.
lines.style: Quieter now, more reverent. He's moving deeper into the past, or deeper into himself. Slower pace. The wistfulness is becoming almost fragile here.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、有楽町の映画館で名画を観たわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather watched classic films at the cinema in Yurakucho, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle but steady. She's meeting him in that deeper place. Not correcting now — confirming, building the monument together. Voice is patient, almost ceremonial.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと三鷹の井の頭公園を歩いた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, I walked with him in Inokashira Park in Mitaka.
lines.style: A pivot — suddenly intimate. This one is *his* memory alone. Slower, quieter. He's not just remembering a detail now, he's remembering a feeling. The walk, the two of them.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、私をダーリンと呼んで下さった日もあったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: There were times when your grandfather called me 'darling,' weren't there, dear?
lines.style: Very quiet now, almost whispered. She's moved past the playful back-and-forth. This is the memory that matters most. Her voice is tender and slightly vulnerable — she's offering him something real.
